question: On 26 May 2026, the President of Ukraine signed Decree No 440/2026, granting a military unit the name ‘Heroes of the UPA’ (Ukrainian Insurgent Army). This formation was responsible for mass crimes against the Polish population, including the genocide in Volhynia, with approximately 100 000–120 000 victims.

This decision has been regarded as promoting the cult of perpetrators of murders of civilians, including women and children, and as evidence of Ukraine’s moral unpreparedness for EU membership. At the same time, the President of the Commission has recently announced ‘decisive steps’ in Ukraine’s accession process.

The glorification of the chauvinistic and criminal ideology of Banderism stands in clear contradiction to the values set out in Article 2 of the Treaty on European Union (TEU). In view of the above: 1.
Does the Commission consider that the official commemoration by a candidate state of a formation responsible for genocide is incompatible with the EU values enshrined in Article 2 TEU?
Does the Commission intend to officially condemn the resurgence of Ukrainian chauvinism and make further negotiations conditional upon Kyiv completely ceasing the glorification of war criminals?
Does the Commission still seek the rapid accession of Ukraine to the EU in a situation where its historical policy strikes at deep sensitivities and the remembrance of victims in Member States?
answer: The EU is founded on the values set out in Article 2 of the Treaty on European Union, including respect for human dignity, human rights, democracy, equality and the rights of persons belonging to minorities. These values also underpin the accession process.

The Commission assesses compliance of Ukraine with the accession criteria on the basis of the established framework, including the political criteria relating to the stability of institutions guaranteeing democracy, the rule of law, human rights and respect for and protection of minorities. The Commission reports regularly on Ukraine’s progress in the context of the enlargement process.

Issues pertaining to the massacres of Polish civilians in Volhynia and Eastern Galicia, as well as related questions of historical memory, remembrance policies and commemorative practices should be addressed in a spirit of dialogue, responsibility and good neighbourly relations.

In this context, the Commission encourages and supports all efforts aimed at genuine reconciliation, and at the dignified and respectful commemoration of the Polish victims. The Commission will continue to assess Ukraine’s overall compliance with the accession criteria in line with the established methodology for enlargement.
